Measuring Risk Aversion

Raise the risk-aversion coefficient γ\gammaγ in CRRA utility and the certainty equivalent drifts away from the expected value — the risk premium grows. The Arrow-Pratt measure reads off alongside.

u(x)=x1−γ1−γu(x) = \frac{x^{1-\gamma}}{1-\gamma}u(x)=1−γx1−γ​
rA(x)=−u′′(x)u′(x)=γxr_A(x) = -\frac{u''(x)}{u'(x)} = \frac{\gamma}{x}rA​(x)=−u′(x)u′′(x)​=xγ​

Examples & Exercises

In CRRA utility, γ=1\gamma = 1γ=1 is log utility u(x)=ln⁡xu(x) = \ln xu(x)=lnx. For the 50-50 lottery (150,50)(150, 50)(150,50), find the certainty equivalent and the risk premium, and compute the Arrow-Pratt absolute risk aversion rA(100)r_A(100)rA​(100).

ln⁡c=12ln⁡150+12ln⁡50=ln⁡150⋅50\ln c = \tfrac{1}{2}\ln 150 + \tfrac{1}{2}\ln 50 = \ln\sqrt{150 \cdot 50}lnc=21​ln150+21​ln50=ln150⋅50​
rA(x)=−u′′(x)u′(x)=1xr_A(x) = -\frac{u''(x)}{u'(x)} = \frac{1}{x}rA​(x)=−u′(x)u′′(x)​=x1​
Show proof
  1. From ln⁡c=12ln⁡150+12ln⁡50=ln⁡150⋅50=ln⁡7500\ln c = \frac{1}{2}\ln 150 + \frac{1}{2}\ln 50 = \ln\sqrt{150 \cdot 50} = \ln\sqrt{7500}lnc=21​ln150+21​ln50=ln150⋅50​=ln7500​ we get c=7500≈86.60c = \sqrt{7500} \approx 86.60c=7500​≈86.60. The risk premium is 100−86.60=13.40100 - 86.60 = 13.40100−86.60=13.40.
  2. With u(x)=ln⁡xu(x) = \ln xu(x)=lnx, u′(x)=1/xu'(x) = 1/xu′(x)=1/x and u′′(x)=−1/x2u''(x) = -1/x^2u′′(x)=−1/x2. Hence rA(x)=−u′′(x)/u′(x)=1/xr_A(x) = -u''(x)/u'(x) = 1/xrA​(x)=−u′′(x)/u′(x)=1/x, and rA(100)=0.01r_A(100) = 0.01rA​(100)=0.01. This matches the CRRA formula rA(x)=γ/xr_A(x) = \gamma/xrA​(x)=γ/x at γ=1\gamma = 1γ=1.

Show that the CRRA consumer is risk neutral at γ=0\gamma = 0γ=0: find the certainty equivalent and the risk premium of the 50-50 lottery (150,50)(150, 50)(150,50).

u(x)=x1−01−0=xu(x) = \frac{x^{1-0}}{1-0} = xu(x)=1−0x1−0​=x
Show proof
  1. At γ=0\gamma = 0γ=0, u(x)=x1/1=xu(x) = x^{1}/1 = xu(x)=x1/1=x — linear utility. Expected utility is U(L)=12⋅150+12⋅50=100=E[L]U(L) = \frac{1}{2} \cdot 150 + \frac{1}{2} \cdot 50 = 100 = \mathbb{E}[L]U(L)=21​⋅150+21​⋅50=100=E[L].
  2. The certainty equivalent is c=U(L)=100c = U(L) = 100c=U(L)=100, so the risk premium is 100−100=0100 - 100 = 0100−100=0. Also rA(x)=γ/x=0r_A(x) = \gamma/x = 0rA​(x)=γ/x=0 — the Arrow-Pratt measure confirms risk neutrality. In the figure the normalized curve coincides with the chord and the Jensen gap vanishes.
